newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Mar 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Mar 19.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
One Indian national was killed in a gunbattle with police in in the border town of Chowgacha on Tuesday.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Tuesday said a comprehensive water policy to ensure optimum utilisation of water resources was in the offing.
Opposition leader and the former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia on Tuesday said the country's "sovereign identity and independence" were under threat at the hands of the ruling Awami League.
Frozen shrimps worth about 3 billion taka may rot away if power failures to fish processing plants in Khulna continues.
The U.S. House of Representative has called upon the international financial institutions and the international community to extend help in Bangladesh's efforts for poverty alleviation.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina leaves Dhaka for Islamabad on Saturday to attend a summit of the Organisation of Islamic Conference (OIC) scheduled for March 23.
The Tk 200 million Kailashtila Liquified Petroleum Gas (LPG) plant in Sylhet is expected to go into production in July.
Former Prsident Hussain Mohammad Ershad on Tuesday said his Jatiya Party opposed any idea to allow India to use Chittagong Port.
